doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: Welcome and the biggest changes in music
summary: Rowe welcomes the two guests; Gallodoro says the greatest change is that good music and standards have declined.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. And it’s our great pleasure to have two wonderful musical gentlemen and really all around great guys I’ve been able to discover, Al Gallodoro, saxophonist and clarinetist, and Mr. Spiegle Willcox, trombonist. Welcome gentlemen. It’s a great pleasure to be here with you.
Incidentally, thank you for pronouncing my name correctly.

And you made sure I did. You have one of those names that’s easy to misspell. You know I’ve been thinking, in listening to you talk, your lives have seen some great changes, not only musically, but everything. Is there some things that occur to you— that’s kind of a hard question because there’s so many things, but what are some of the greatest things that you have witnessed in your life?
The greatest changes is, in general music has gone down. The good music, the good standards, you know. Now shall I start back from 1927?
